displayedInputs.question:
In the diagram below, a diameter of each of the two smaller circles is a radius of the larger circle. If the two smaller circles have a combined area of \(1\) square unit, then what is the area of the shaded region, in square units?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In a sign pyramid a cell gets a “+” if the two cells below it have the same sign, and it gets a “-” if the two cells below it have different signs. The diagram below illustrates a sign pyramid with four levels. How many possible ways are there to fill the four cells in the bottom row to produce a “+” at the top of the pyramid?

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

In \(\triangle ABC,\) a point \(E\) is on \(\overline{AB}\) with \(AE=1\) and \(EB=2.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overline{AC}\) so that \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\) and point \(F\) is on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(\overline{EF} \parallel \overline{AC}.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(CDEF\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Point \(E\) is the midpoint of side \(\overline{CD}\) in square \(ABCD,\) and \(\overline{BE}\) meets diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) at \(F.\) The area of quadrilateral \(AFED\) is \(45.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

From a regular octagon, a triangle is formed by connecting three randomly chosen vertices of the octagon. What is the probability that at least one of the sides of the triangle is also a side of the octagon?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

In the cube \(ABCDEFGH\) with opposite vertices \(C\) and \(E,\) \(J\) and \(I\) are the midpoints of edges \(\overline{FB}\) and \(\overline{HD},\) respectively. Let \(R\) be the ratio of the area of the cross-section \(EJCI\) to the area of one of the faces of the cube. What is \(R^2?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

The figure below shows line \(\ell\) with a regular, infinite, recurring pattern of squares and line segments.

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

How many of the following four kinds of rigid motion transformations of the plane in which this figure is drawn, other than the identity transformation, will transform this figure into itself?

• some rotation around a point of line \(\ell\)

• some translation in the direction parallel to line \(\ell\)

• the reflection across line \(\ell\)

• some reflection across a line perpendicular to line \(\ell\)

The figure below shows \(13\) circles of radius \(1\) within a larger circle. All the intersections occur at points of tangency. What is the area of the region, shaded in the figure, inside the larger circle but outside all the circles of radius \(1?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: Each smaller circle has half the larger circle's radius. The shaded area is the larger disk's area minus the two smaller disks' combined area.
mappings.answerReason: Let each smaller radius be r. Then 2πr²=1 and the larger radius is 2r. The shaded area is π(2r)²−2πr²=2πr²=1.

mappings.rationale: Encoding the signs as +1 and −1 makes the cell rule multiplication. Three bottom signs can be chosen freely, after which the required top sign uniquely determines the fourth.
mappings.answerReason: For bottom signs a,b,c,d, the next rows are ab,bc,cd and then ac,bd, so the top is abcd. Each of the 2³ choices of a,b,c requires exactly one choice d=abc to produce +1. Thus there are 8 fillings.

mappings.rationale: The parallel segments produce two triangles similar to ABC. Their squared similarity ratios give the area fractions to subtract from the whole triangle.
mappings.answerReason: AB=3. Triangle ADE has similarity ratio AE/AB=1/3, while triangle EBF has ratio EB/AB=2/3. Therefore area(CDEF)/area(ABC)=1−(1/3)²−(2/3)²=4/9.

mappings.rationale: Subtracting triangle FCE from triangle ADC relates AFED to the square's area. The position of F can be obtained either from similar triangles ABF and CEF or from coordinate line equations.
mappings.answerReason: Since AB is parallel to CE and AB=2CE, similarity gives AF=2CF. For square side s, F is therefore s/3 above CD. Thus area(FCE)=(1/2)(s/2)(s/3)=s²/12, and area(AFED)=s²/2−s²/12=5s²/12=45. Hence s²=108.

mappings.rationale: The equally likely outcomes are unordered three-vertex subsets. Favorable triangles can be counted by separating those containing exactly one octagon side from those containing two.
mappings.answerReason: There are C(8,3)=56 triangles. Exactly two octagon sides occur in the 8 consecutive-vertex triples. For exactly one side, choose that side in 8 ways and the third vertex in 4 ways, giving 32. The probability is (8+32)/56=5/7.

mappings.rationale: Face right triangles show that all four section sides are equal, making EJCI a rhombus. Pythagorean calculations give its diagonals, whose product determines its area.
mappings.answerReason: For cube edge s, each section side has length √(s²+(s/2)²), so the section is a rhombus. Its diagonals are EC=s√3 and JI=s√2. Its area is s²√6/2, so R=√6/2 and R²=3/2.

mappings.rationale: The task tests whether the entire recurring pattern is preserved by translation, reflection, and a half-turn. The alternating square positions and attached diagonal segments distinguish the possible symmetries.
mappings.answerReason: A translation by one full repeat preserves the figure. A 180° rotation about the point of ℓ halfway between neighboring upper and lower squares also preserves it. Reflection across ℓ or any perpendicular line reverses the diagonal attachments' slope, so neither reflection works. Exactly 2 listed kinds qualify.

mappings.rationale: Tangency fixes adjacent unit-circle centers 2 units apart. The staggered rows form isosceles center triangles whose heights determine the outer radius; the shaded area then follows by subtracting thirteen unit-disk areas.
mappings.answerReason: By the displayed symmetry, the large circle is centered at the middle unit circle's center. Each row gap is √(2²−1²)=√3, so the top unit-circle center is 2√3 above it. The outer radius is 1+2√3. Thus the shaded area is π(1+2√3)²−13π=4π√3.
